content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. I did not compare it against the original lodash code at runtime, because lodash isn't installed here. Instead I checked es-toolkit's behaviour by hand against lodash's known behaviour.

The `tsc` errors are all in `src/module.ts` (it can't find the `lodash/*` modules), and none are in `out/module.ts`. I didn't re-run `tsc` on `out/` alone, so type checking of the new file is not confirmed.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 701 bytes (min+gzip) in total, with 87 bytes of my own code. I couldn't measure the original's size for comparison.

| Function | Before | After | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `lodash/words` | `words` from `es-toolkit` | Same output on all 12 test strings (digit boundaries, consecutive capitals, `_`, `-`, `.`, trailing space, empty). |
| `byAge` | `groupBy(rows, 'age')` | `groupBy` from `es-toolkit`, `(row) => row.age` | es-toolkit's strict version takes a key function, not a property name. That is the only adapter. Keys come out as strings, as in lodash. |
| `isBlank` | `lodash/isEmpty` | `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat` | es-toolkit has no strict `isEmpty`, so compat is the only es-toolkit option. It returns true for numbers and booleans and false for non-empty arrays and objects, the same as lodash. |

Lodash is no longer imported. I installed nothing and created no other source files.

Docs for `isEmpty`: https://es-toolkit.dev/compat/reference/predicate/isEmpty.html
